frontmatter.title: Noncommuting Lindblad dynamics
frontmatter.description: Explicit Lie/Strang channel circuits for a one-qubit Hamiltonian and damping jump.

children.value: This example combines a Hamiltonian rotation with amplitude damping. Their generators do not commute, so alternating exact substeps introduces a controlled splitting approximation. It extends the
with an actual quantum channel circuit for the combined dynamics.

First- and second-order positive-time splitting circuits are implemented and compared with a small independently assembled Liouvillian exponential. Hamiltonian substeps use an exact analytic RY–RZ–RY construction; damping substeps use the checked environment dilation with a fresh reset each time. Original gates, resets, input preparation and final readout are counted. General interacting Lindblad simulation, continuous-angle synthesis, physical estimates and formal certificates remain planned.

children.value: Thus Lie applies H then damping chronologically; Strang applies half H, damping and half H. Every substep duration is nonnegative, and each substep is a valid quantum channel. Lie–Trotter and symmetric Strang splitting provide the algorithmic context
. Liouvillian product-formula theory is discussed by Kliesch et al., together with its erratum
; the numerical curves here are implementation evidence.

Each damping step resets the environment to zero, then applies the survival-aware controlled-RY/reverse-CX dilation from the damping example. Resetting the reused environment discards its previous correlations. Keeping the old environment would implement a correlated repeated interaction instead of the intended Markovian composition; a test checks that removing these resets changes the result.

children.value: value meets the proposed 0.01 splitting allowance numerically. This is a toy-instance numerical check, not a formal interval or diamond-norm certificate.
Sampling error 0.03 and statistical failure probability 0.005 give a Hoeffding proposal of

. That budget applies to one fixed Z mean; X/Y tomography, other initial states, different times and multiple settings require separate confidence allocations. The ledger’s seeded ideal-probability draw is illustrative.

Physical-fault probability is separately proposed at 0.005 across all trials. Continuous-angle synthesis is still pending. A conservative synthesis proposal uses the sum of primitive-gate operator errors and contraction under intervening channel/discard operations; it does not supply a certified Clifford+T sequence. Representation rounding, outer splitting, coherent synthesis, statistical confidence and physical faults are distinct quantities.

Classical coefficient/angle preparation and readout wall time, physical reset/discard/measurement duration, routing, factories and error correction are excluded from the logical ledger. The current static physical adapter rejects mid-circuit resets; a reset/instrument-aware physical model is required before projecting this full workload. No physical estimate or improvement over the frozen baseline is claimed.
